prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the camera wearer’s red-clad torso and arms as the nearest surfaces, roughly 0–0.5 m away, from the seated or crouched person ahead at approximately 0.7–1.5 m; the floor, wall, and other standing people are generally farther away, around 1.5–3+ m. The other person remains mostly in front of the wearer and slightly left or right depending on the frame, while peripheral legs and bodies are farther left or behind them; the wearer’s arms repeatedly occlude parts of the person and scene. Across frames 1–4, the central person stays at a broadly similar range while the camera rotates or shifts around them; in frame 5, the wearer’s near arm crosses much of the right foreground and the person appears more toward the upper-right and slightly farther away. This map makes near-versus-far layering and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB, but its smooth tonal transitions do not support precise metre estimates and appear unreliable around limbs, image edges, the measuring tape, and merged body surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies several person regions: the camera wearer occupies a very large foreground mask, the seated or crouched person lies directly ahead within roughly 1 m, and fragments of additional people appear near the left, upper, or side boundaries at greater distances. It clarifies which overlapping patches belong to people when arms, legs, and torsos occlude one another, including people partly outside the field of view; however, it supplies no dependable metric depth, so distances come mainly from mask size, overlap, and the RGB context. Across the five frames, the wearer’s mask shifts from the centre-right foreground to a broad right-side occluder, while the person ahead moves across the central area toward the upper-right as the viewpoint turns; small peripheral person masks enter and leave the borders. The map is unreliable where one person is split into multiple islands, adjacent people receive similar colours, body parts merge with unrelated cyan regions, and many objects—including the floor, wall, clothing details, and measuring tape—remain unlabeled.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides almost no usable structure in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, but frame 3 contains a sparse yellow skeleton near the centre, corresponding to an upper body or arm arrangement roughly 0.5–1.5 m in front of the camera. Its connected joints show relative geometry more clearly than RGB: one limb extends upward, another runs mainly left-to-right, and several small points cluster to the left, but the detection is too incomplete to determine a full-body stance, reliable facing direction, eye contact, or exact reach. The visible joints indicate that some detected limbs are approximately level with one another while one endpoint is higher, and overlapping lines reveal articulation despite clothing and partial occlusion. Because most people and frames have no detected skeleton, and the lone skeleton has missing or possibly misassigned joints, this map is unreliable for tracking approach, retreat, turning, inter-person distance, or what is within anyone’s arm’s reach.
